gancho: On Kauaʻi, Hiʻiaka fights two moʻo women on a cliff, finds Lohiʻau's spirit inside a little coconut shell, and chants for ten days to bring him back to life. But the forty days are long gone, and at Kīlauea, Pele breaks her oath: she burns Hiʻiaka's lehua forest and turns her best friend Hōpoe into stone. Based on N. B. Emerson, Pele and Hiiaka (1915), W. D. Westervelt (1916) and Martha Beckwith (1940).
